name: Automobile
rationale: The auto sector depends on supplier ecosystems (small suppliers, industrial areas), skilled workers and power, plus logistics to ports for exports.

name: Electronics
rationale: Needs skilled workers and stable power above all, plugged into existing industrial areas and import/export links.

name: General Manufacturing
rationale: A balanced profile: an existing industrial base, power and connectivity. Also covers printing and packaging, which follow the manufacturing base.

name: Textile & Apparel
rationale: Powerloom and garment clusters are led by small units and are power-hungry; processing needs water; spinning is linked to cotton output.

name: Sugar & Ethanol
rationale: Mills and distilleries must sit close to irrigated cane fields; cane is bulky, so road and rail haulage matter, and ethanol ships to oil-company depots by rail.

name: Dairy
rationale: Fodder-rich irrigated farm belts supply milk; chilling needs power and water; collection needs roads.

name: Food & Beverages
rationale: Diverse, high-output farm supply, plus water (bottling is water-first), power and market access.

name: Agro & Cold Storage
rationale: Primary processing (milling, grading) and cold stores close to production, with power for refrigeration.

name: Pharmaceuticals
rationale: Formulation and API plants need a skilled, graduate workforce, clean process water and uninterrupted power, inside existing industrial areas with export links.

name: Chemicals
rationale: Chemical units use large volumes of water, import feedstock through ports and must sit in notified chemical zones; bulk inputs move by rail.

name: Plastics & Rubber
rationale: Moulding, extrusion and tyre plants are power-intensive, sit in large industrial areas near auto makers, and import polymer granules, natural rubber and carbon black through ports.

name: Logistics & Warehousing
rationale: Warehousing lives on connectivity: national highways, rail freight and port access, plus affordable land for large sheds.
